spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Serving a neural network at batch size 1 leaves modern GPUs (A100/H100) 80–90% idle because streaming weights from HBM into SRAM dominates compute time.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Iteration-Level LLM Batching (Zero Head-of-Line Blocking) (PREFILL CHUNK -> DECODE STEP -> EOS EJECT); Prefix-Aware Router -> Continuous Batching Engine -> Paged KV HBM (Prefix Router -> vLLM Scheduler -> Paged KV Blocks -> Tensor Cores).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Match the batching scheduler to model architecture and TTFT/ITL SLOs. At scale, an L7 inference router uses **prefix-cache-aware consistent routing** to steer repeated system-prompt prefixes to the same vLLM replica (maximizing RadixAttention/APC.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore PagedAttention, speculative decoding, FlashAttention, and quantization.

learningJourney.title: What is GPU Inference Batching

explanation.foundation: Serving a neural network at batch size 1 leaves modern GPUs (A100/H100) 80–90% idle because streaming weights from HBM into SRAM dominates compute time.
explanation.core: **Batching** amortizes one HBM weight read across $B$ inputs, raising **arithmetic intensity (FLOPs/byte)** toward the GPU's roofline and multiplying throughput 5–20x per GPU.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Model Serving & GPU Batching, watch how what is gpu inference batching interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. learningJourney.title: Why Static Batching causes Head-of-Line Blocking & Decode Stutter

explanation.foundation: Think of **Why Static Batching causes Head-of-Line Blocking & Decode Stutter** as the intuition layer for Model Serving & GPU Batching: The problem: see what breaks without Why Static Batching causes Head-of-Line Blocking & Decode Stutter under real concurrency or scale.
explanation.core:
Two failure modes wreck tail latency in naive GPU servers:
- **Head-of-Line (HoL) Blocking**: in static request-level batches, one 4,096-token generation stalls 15 already-finished 64-token requests, spiking p99 10x.
- **Prefill-Decode Interference**: a 16k-token prompt prefill hogs GPU SMs for 400 ms, causing visible streaming stutter (`ITL > 200 ms`) for all active decode users.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, why static batching causes head-of-line blocking & decode stutter becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Group concurrent inference requests into tensor batches on the GPU to shift workloads from memory-bandwidth-bound to compute-bound without blowing tail latency.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Model Serving & GPU Batching without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, use dynamic batching with a tight queue timeout (2–10 ms) for fixed-shape encoders, and iteration-level continuous batching with PagedAttention for autoregressive LLMs.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Dynamic Batching (Triton) & Continuous Batching (vLLM)

explanation.core: Set tight `max_queue_delay_microseconds` (2–10 ms) for encoders in Triton, and enable `enable_chunked_prefill` + `max_num_batched_tokens` in vLLM for LLMs.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, dynamic batching (triton) & continuous batching (vllm) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. learningJourney.markdownContent:
```protobuf
# NVIDIA Triton config.pbtxt for fixed-shape embedding/vision encoders
dynamic_batching {
  preferred_batch_size: [ 8, 16, 32 ]
  max_queue_delay_microseconds: 5000  # 5 ms ceiling on queue wait
}
```

```bash
# vLLM continuous batching with chunked prefill to protect decode ITL
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 128
```

benefits: Simple to configure for fixed-compute encoders, embeddings, and vision models.
costs: Causes severe HoL blocking on variable-length autoregressive LLMs.

benefits: Zero HoL blocking; high KV-cache memory utilization via 16-token pages.
costs: Complex block-table scheduler; long prefills still contend with decodes unless chunked.

benefits: Eliminates prefill-decode interference completely by isolating compute-bound prefill from bandwidth-bound decode.
costs: Requires fast RDMA/NVLink KV-cache transfer between prefill and decode GPUs.
